summary: Outputs Oculus Rift HMD/controller orientation, acceleration, velocity, device info, and eye projection matrices for VR integration.
key_concepts: Oculus Rift CHOP is a Windows-only Oculus Rift interface for HMD, controller, and projection-matrix channel data.
Output selects HMD, left or right controller, or left or right eye projection-matrix modes.
The CHOP can output orientation, acceleration, velocity, angular velocity, device info, and controller button channels.
Recenter resets position and yaw from the current HMD pose and is used to align the virtual origin with the user.
Projection matrix output is intended for Camera COMP custom projection parameters in stereo rendering setups.
When no Oculus Rift is attached, the docs describe default developer-kit-style channels for development/testing.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Update Oculus data when the CHOP cooks

key_params.name: output
key_params.note: HMD, controller, or eye-projection-matrix output mode

key_params.name: recenter
key_params.note: Reset positional components and yaw orientation using current HMD pose

key_params.name: near
key_params.note: Near clip distance for projection matrix

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

common_gotchas: Official docs list this operator as Windows-only.
Projection matrix channels must be passed into a camera Custom Projection parameter for proper stereo rendering.
Prediction can reduce apparent latency by estimating future orientation, but generated plans should make prediction timing explicit.
Without an Oculus Rift connected, default developer-kit-style channels are output for design/testing only.
Calibration/projection values may differ on future devices and should not be treated as stable across headsets.
Use Oculus Rift TOP or newer OpenVR/OpenXR-style workflows when the rendering path needs headset-specific output.
